hero.h1: Bathroom Remodeling in Puyallup, WA, Built Right Behind the Walls
hero.subheadline: Brad Zemke is a third-generation carpenter and Air Force veteran. His own crew handles demo, plumbing, waterproofing and tile, and you get a fixed price before work starts.

image.alt: Bathroom remodeling Puyallup WA: primary bath with a freestanding soaking tub, frameless glass corner shower, skylight and wood-look plank floor

intro.h2: The work behind the walls matters
paragraphs: Pacific Remodeling has offered bathroom remodeling in Puyallup, WA since Brad Zemke started the company in 2018, after five years as a B-52 crew chief in the Air Force. His grandfather and father were carpenters too. Brad says he has renovated hundreds of bathrooms across Pierce County, from 40-square-foot guest baths to 120-square-foot master suites.

What sets his bathrooms apart is the part you never see. Every shower gets a full waterproofing membrane, Schluter KERDI or equivalent, floor to ceiling, and it is inspected before tile goes on. His team does the demolition, plumbing, electrical, tile and finish work in-house, so no stranger subcontractors show up at your door.

services.h2: Bathroom remodeling in Puyallup, WA, plus kitchens and counters

items.name: Full Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Master suites with dual vanities, soaking tubs and heated floors, plus hall baths and powder rooms. Brad publishes real ranges: about $16,000 to $35,000 and 2 to 3 weeks for a hall bath, and $33,000 to $72,000 and 4 to 6 weeks for a mid-range master bath.

image.alt: Bathroom remodel with a white double vanity, quartz top, two framed mirrors with sconces and dark tile floor

items.name: Tub-to-Shower Conversions
items.blurb: The most requested job: about 7 in 10 of Brad's bathroom remodels include one. The old tub comes out, the drain moves, and a custom tile walk-in shower goes in with niches and frameless glass. A standard conversion runs $10,000 to $24,000 and takes 1 to 2 weeks.

image.alt: Tub-to-shower conversion with marble-look porcelain walls, recessed niche, rain head and sliding frameless glass door

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Open layouts, real-wood cabinetry, quartz counters and new flooring. Brad prefers maple for painted cabinets because it resists warping in the damp Pacific Northwest. Cabinetry for a typical Puyallup kitchen with 25 to 35 linear feet runs about $20,000 to $56,000.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with sage green beadboard cabinets, herringbone marble backsplash, stainless hood and granite counters

items.name: Countertops
items.blurb: Granite, quartz, marble and butcher block, templated, cut and installed with tight seams and solid support. A straightforward replacement takes 2 to 3 weeks from consultation to install, and sinks and faucets are reconnected the same day so you have a working kitchen by evening.

image.alt: White shaker kitchen with speckled quartz counters, subway tile backsplash, open shelves and dark wood floor

why_choose_us.h2: Why Pierce County homeowners hire Brad

items.title: Prices on the page
items.text: Brad lists real cost ranges and timelines for powder rooms, hall baths, master baths and conversions, and his written proposal is fixed-price with every line item spelled out.

items.title: One crew, no strangers
items.text: Demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, tile and finish work are done by Pacific Remodeling's own crews, which means fewer scheduling gaps and one person accountable.

items.title: Waterproofing is not optional
items.text: Every shower gets a Schluter KERDI or RedGard membrane on every wall, floor, curb and niche. Brad has torn out five-year-old showers that leaked because someone skipped this step.

items.title: Reviewers trust Brad
items.text: Google reviewers mention Brad by name, a respectful crew and an easy process. One couple chose him after interviewing five companies for their bathroom remodel.

about.h2: Meet Brad Zemke, owner and carpenter
about.text: Brad Zemke comes from a family of carpenters: his grandfather and his father both worked the trade. He spent five years as a B-52 crew chief in the Air Force, then started Pacific Remodeling in Puyallup in 2018 and brought that same discipline to every job. With more than 20 years in the trades, Brad still runs projects himself and walks every finished room with the homeowner. His rule for every job is simple: if this were his mom's house, how would he want it done? Pacific Remodeling is licensed, bonded and insured in Washington.

image.alt: Brad Zemke, owner of Pacific Remodeling in Puyallup, WA

process.h2: From first call to final walkthrough

steps.title: Free in-home consultation
steps.text: Brad visits, measures and talks through what you want and what you can spend. It usually takes 45 to 60 minutes, with no sales pitch.

steps.title: Fixed-price proposal
steps.text: Within about a week you get a detailed proposal with materials, labor, scope and timeline spelled out line by line.

steps.title: Selections
steps.text: Brad helps you pick tile, vanity, fixtures, counters and hardware, and will visit showrooms with you if needed.

steps.title: Build with daily updates
steps.text: Dust barriers go up on day one. Rough-in and waterproofing are inspected before walls close, and the crew cleans up every day.

steps.title: Final walkthrough
steps.text: Brad walks every inch of the finished room with you. If anything is not right, it gets fixed before the job is called done.

service_area.h2: Puyallup home base, all of Pierce County
service_area.text: Puyallup is home base, and Brad has done more projects here than anywhere else. The crew also works across Pierce County, from Tacoma's North End and West Side to newer homes around Lake Tapps and Bonney Lake, the growing developments in Sumner, larger lots in Edgewood and the neighborhoods of South Hill. The service menu also lists Orting, Buckley, University Place, Lakewood, Fife, Milton and Spanaway.

items.q: How much does a bathroom remodel cost in Puyallup?
items.a: Brad's published ranges are $6,500 to $16,000 for a powder room, $10,000 to $29,000 for a tub-to-shower conversion, $16,000 to $35,000 for a full hall bath and $33,000 to $72,000 for a mid-range master bath. These include materials, labor, plumbing, electrical and finish work. Permits are extra when required.

items.q: How long will my bathroom be out of service?
items.a: A powder room update takes about 1 to 2 weeks and a tub-to-shower conversion 1 to 2 weeks. A guest or hall bath runs 2 to 3 weeks, and master baths take 4 to 8 weeks depending on whether the layout changes. Your proposal includes a timeline for your specific project.

Layout, plumbing and electrical changes usually do. Brad pulls permits from the City of Puyallup and schedules the inspections. Permit fees typically run $250 to $800 and are added to the project price when required. Rough-in work and waterproofing are inspected before any walls are closed or tile is set.

items.q: Can you make a bathroom safer for aging in place?
items.a: Yes. Brad builds curbless, zero-threshold showers with a linear drain by recessing the shower pan into the subfloor, though some older homes need a slight ramp instead. He also adds solid wood blocking behind the drywall so grab bars can be mounted securely now or years later.

Yes. Brad comes to your home, measures, and talks through materials and budget at no cost and with no obligation. Within about a week you receive a written fixed-price proposal. Call (253) 392-9266, Monday through Saturday from 8 AM to 6 PM, to set a time.
